items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: they had to get in line out there at G&M Studios, which were owned by Cosmo. Cosmo Matias.

ctx.x: When record companies would come from Montana in the 1950s, and people would hear, tell me that story about how people would come to the studio to audition. What the audition process was?

Well, both the songwriters and the singers, they had to get in line out there at G&M Studios, which were owned by Cosmo. Cosmo Matias. Cosmo Matias. Cosmo Matias. And they were getting in line. It could be raining. You think they're looking at a gong to wind or something out there. That could be songwriters and artists trying to say, hey, they're getting in line to audition. And they got this guy and they're standing up saying, okay, sing something. And you sing about one, two, three balls. And you know, next,…

Excuse me. Before we run out of time, they might want to hear him sing something. I'd like to get the mic a little closer. I guess that's him, okay? So is Varsity pickup? I'm sure it's on, Dusty. I'm hoping there's some questions. Yeah, they may have some questions too, because they closed the building down. That might be a little closer to your bar. It's another one. It's good. How much time do you have? Oh, it has to be. Is there? Yeah. Let's do that. I hate for them not to have a chance to get any questions…
